newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-YOUTH AND EXPERIENCE BATTLE FOR PLACE IN THE FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-YOUTH AND EXPERIENCE BATTLE FOR PLACE IN THE FINAL.

text.p: Two 16-year-old tennis prodigies, top seed Martina Hingis and ice-cool Russian Anna Kournikova, battle it out on Thursday for their first taste of a Wimbledon final.
In Saturday's showdown one or the other will meet a highly-experienced Wimbledon hand in Jana Novotna or Arantxa Sanchez Vicario, both of whom know the pain of falling at the last hurdle.
Hingis, who has shot to the top of the rankings in the past six months with a triumph at the Australian Open and only one defeat this year, was always expected to get this far.
But Kournikova, whom Hingis beat 6-1 6-3 on red clay at the French Open last month, has stunned and delighted the Wimbledon crowd with her power and grace on the grass court.
"On this surface she feels much more confident," Hingis said of her opponent, who turned 16 three weeks ago some eight months after the Czech-born Swiss.
"She's improving by each match so for sure it's going to be a tough one for me", Hingis added.

Kournikova, schooled in Florida by Nick Bollettieri, who also produced Andre Agassi and Monica Seles, has been taken to three sets in three rounds of the tournament, but she has shown immense self-belief to battle through.
In the quarter-finals her inch-perfect shots and speed about the court earned her a prized 7-6 6-3 win over French Open champion Iva Majoli of Croatia.
She then went on to play a long women's doubles match with Elena Likhovtseva which she lost and during which she needed courtside treatment from a physiotherapist.
"I'm feeling a little bit tired," she confessed. "I have a sore left hip." The soreness forced her to pull out of a mixed doubles match also scheduled for Wednesday.

Hingis, by contrast, is fresh as a daisy. She has not dropped a set on her way to the semifinals and sped through her quarter-final against Denisa Chladkova 6-3 6-2. She then went on to win the final set of a doubles match held over from Tuesday -- a brief and successful jaunt on an outside court alongside Sanchez Vicario.
Success does not surprise her. "I've always worked hard for it, so that I could achieve anything," she said. Maybe it's more of a surprise for other people."
Whichever teenager reaches the final will be the youngest to get there since the All England club finally opened its doors to professionals as well as amateurs in 1968.
Steffi Graf, who has ruled Wimbledon for a decade, but is injured this year, was already 18 when she played her first Wimbledon final in 1987.
All of which must make Novotna, 28 and veteran of 12 championships and Sanchez Vicario, 25, a survivor of 11, feel rather ancient.

Sanchez Vicario lost the last two Wimbledon finals to Graf and the German also accounted for Novotna in 1993, when the Czech threw away a 4-1 lead in the final set and then wept as she received the runners-up trophy.

Though she hit a bad patch earlier this year with few wins and a drop in rankings, Sanchez Vicario has looked very secure this Wimbledon, losing only 20 games and no sets on her way to the semifinals.
She trounced ninth seed Mary Pierce 6-1 6-3 in the fourth round and swept past Nathalie Tauziat 6-2 7-5 on Wednesday.

The Spaniard, who runs down every ball and never says die, already has a U.S. and two French Opens to her name. She is anxious to add the Wimbledon crown and with four wins apiece against each other in singles tournaments she and Novotna look evenly matched.
The pair used to play doubles together but fell out and have since become keen rivals.
Novotna has a natural grass court game and should have won here years ago but for her fragile temperament. This season, however, she has been remarkably solid.

"Coming into this tournament I was feeling very confident," she said. "I'm just looking forward to it -- not looking at it for the point of view that it's Wimbledon, it's semifinal or something like that," she added.
"I will go out there and enjoy myself and entertain the crowd because that's what tennis is all about."
